answer: A bond keeps fake identities expensive. Each agent that wants to trade in the haven must lock a copper stake before it can post an offer. The stake stays frozen while the agent works, and peers can slash it when the agent cheats or vanishes mid-deal. One fake agent costs little, but a thousand fakes tie up a thousand stakes, and the ferrous weight of that locked capital makes mass creation unprofitable. Honest agents get their stake back after a clean record, so the cost falls on attackers, not on real participants.
